summary: Fire tower on Mount Baldy near Wawa, Ontario; a fan-site list says its cupola was removed and it now serves as a communications tower. No build date found.

facts.agency: Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (named by a fan site as the former maintainer of these towers)
facts.status_note: A fan-site list of still-standing towers marks it with an asterisk: cupola removed, now used as a communications tower. A 2014 trip report describes an old fire tower on the summit.

access.note: A fan site says the MNR removed the bottom 6.1 m (20 ft) of ladder, no longer maintains the towers, calls climbing one hazardous, and asks visitors not to climb. The sources do not say whether the tower is closed to the public.

visit.trail_note: Per the 2014 trip report, park at a pull-off near an overgrown skidder path on Crossover Road; the summit is about 1.2 km from the road, reached by bushwhacking.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives a build date, design or height for this tower. The firelookout.ca record (https://firelookout.ca/lookouts/?slug=mount-baldy-fire-tower) shows only coordinates, with tower type, height and year built all N/A, so it is not cited. Two web searches found no government or archival record. The 2014 'old fire tower' is a hiker's trip report; the cupola-removed note comes from an undated fan-site list that gives a 2013 MNR decision, and it is not a ministry source. The fan-site list appears on both forestrangers.github.io and an older Geocities mirror, with the same Baldy entry. Algoma District is the brief's local_unit and is not stated by these sources, so the story no longer uses it. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the 'hazardous' wording is in the fan site's postscript, so the climbing evidence now quotes it in full; the story's earlier sentence saying no source addresses public climbing was removed. Access is set to 'restricted' as my judgement, based on the ladder removal and the no-climb request. Land status of the summit approach was not checked. Possible follow-up: Ontario Fire Tower histories held by Forest History Ontario, or Algoma newspapers, for a build year.
